name: GitHub Copilot cloud agent, Actions runner
description: A GitHub Copilot cloud agent session that runs on a GitHub Actions runner instead of a cloud sandbox, where copilot-setup-steps.yml, larger runners and self-hosted runners apply. It works one repository, one branch and one pull request for at most 59 minutes. Facts re-read from docs.github.com on the checked date; where the pages disagree, the rule is unconfirmed.

rules.summary: Nothing in the repository delivers the plugin to an Actions session: .github/copilot/settings.json does not enable it, its components are not committed where the cloud agent loads them, and dotfiles do not apply to Actions sessions.
rules.remedy: Commit the skills under .github/skills (or .claude/skills, .agents/skills) and the agents as .github/agents/<name>.agent.md, or enable the plugin in .github/copilot/settings.json. Whether an Actions session loads either is unconfirmed (see repository-components-unconfirmed and plugin-settings-unconfirmed).

rules.summary: The repository enables the plugin in .github/copilot/settings.json, which the agent settings page documents for Copilot in the cloud. Whether an Actions session loads it is unconfirmed: the comparison of Actions and sandbox sessions lists custom instructions, MCP servers and content exclusions for Actions, and the hooks reference says the cloud agent ships with no installed plugins.
rules.remedy: Start an Actions session and check that the plugin's skills are offered; record the result here as basis: observed. Committing the skills under .github/skills is the alternative.

rules.summary: The plugin's skills and agents are committed where the cloud agent loads repository components. Whether an Actions session loads them is unconfirmed: the skills docs say the cloud agent does, but the comparison of Actions and sandbox sessions does not list skills or agents for Actions.
rules.remedy: Start an Actions session and check that the skills are offered; record the result here as basis: observed.

rules.summary: A plugin's commands/ have no counterpart in the cloud agent: the support matrix has no row for them, and prompt files (.github/prompts/*.prompt.md), the nearest Copilot feature, are not supported on GitHub.com.
rules.remedy: Turn the command into a skill (skills/<name>/SKILL.md); a skill is offered where a command would have been typed.
rules.notes: No page says plugin commands are unsupported; the support matrix leaves them out. Observe a plugin command in a session before treating this as fact.

rules.summary: A component spawns subagents with the Agent (Task) tool, declared in its frontmatter or spawned from a fenced Agent(subagent_type: …) call. The customization cheat sheet marks subagents as not supported on GitHub.com, while the custom agents reference maps the agent, custom-agent and Task aliases to 'custom agent' tools in the cloud. The pages disagree.
rules.remedy: Do the subagent's work inline, in the one agent's context, or split it into separate sessions a person starts.
rules.notes: Even if the agent tool works, it invokes a custom agent from .github/agents, not a plugin's agent.

rules.summary: An agent's tools: lists Skill, which the cloud agent does not know and silently drops, so the agent cannot invoke a skill with it.
rules.remedy: Put what the agent needs from the skill in the agent's own instructions, or make the skill the entry point instead of the agent.

rules.summary: An agent's tools: names a tool the cloud agent does not know, such as TaskCreate, or one whose alias the cloud does not support (WebFetch and WebSearch map to web, TodoWrite to todo, both 'currently not applicable for Copilot in the cloud'). All unrecognized names are ignored.
rules.remedy: Drop the name, or use the Copilot alias that covers it (execute, read, edit, search; aliases are case-insensitive). Instructions that rely on the dropped tool need another way to do that step.

rules.summary: A component declares AskUserQuestion. An Actions session is non-interactive: there is nobody to answer.
rules.remedy: Take the answers as arguments or from a committed config file, and report what is missing instead of asking.

rules.summary: In Copilot in the cloud, hook configuration is loaded from .github/hooks/*.json in the cloned repository, and the sandbox does not ship with installed plugins; a plugin's hooks.json is read by the Copilot CLI. An Actions session has no plugin to take them from.
rules.remedy: Port the hook to .github/hooks/<name>.json (version 1 format, bash or command entries only). Claude-style PascalCase event names and matchers are accepted there. A preToolUse command hook is fail-closed: a crash or any non-zero exit denies the tool, not only exit 2, so a hook that exits 1 on its own error starts blocking tools; and a permissionDecision of ask is treated as deny, because no one is there to answer.

rules.summary: A command relies on ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, which no Copilot page documents for the cloud agent. It is probably unset there, and the path collapses to /scripts/….
rules.remedy: Resolve paths from the file's own location (a script's dirname "$0"), or commit what the skill calls into the repository and call it by a repository path.
rules.notes: Re-read on 2026-10-31: the custom agents reference documents ${COPILOT_MCP_*} substitutions in mcp-servers, not ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}; the hooks reference gives the cloud's environment variables without it. Observe it in a session before treating it as fact.

rules.summary: GITHUB_TOKEN is not set in a cloud agent session; GITHUB_COPILOT_GIT_TOKEN and GITHUB_COPILOT_API_TOKEN are.
rules.remedy: Do not read GITHUB_TOKEN. What the agent may do on GitHub is limited anyway (see agent-cannot-git-push and cannot-merge-approve-ready).

rules.summary: The cloud agent pushes to a single branch and can only perform simple push operations; it cannot run git push or other Git commands that need credentials itself.
rules.remedy: Leave committing and pushing to the cloud agent. A flow that owns its branch, pull request and merge does not fit this target.

rules.summary: The cloud agent cannot merge a pull request, approve one, or mark one ready for review.
rules.remedy: End the flow at an open pull request and leave merging, approving and marking ready to a person or a workflow.

rules.summary: By default, workflows on the cloud agent's pull requests do not run until a person with write access clicks Approve and run workflows, so a flow that waits for its own pull request's checks waits for a human. Copilot can be configured to let them run automatically.
rules.remedy: Configure Copilot to allow workflows to run automatically on its pull requests, or do not gate on the checks of a pull request the agent opened and run the checks in the session before pushing instead.

rules.summary: A command runs gh. Whether gh is authenticated in a cloud agent session, and as what, is undocumented.
rules.remedy: Read GitHub through the built-in GitHub MCP server, which is read-only, and leave writes to the cloud agent. Observe gh in a session and record the result here.
rules.notes: Re-read on 2026-10-31: the only gh the Copilot pages mention is gh skill, run locally to install skills.

rules.summary: A component declares a GitHub MCP tool that writes. The cloud agent's built-in GitHub MCP server uses a token with read-only access to the current repository; wider access needs a personal access token or GitHub App configured for it.
rules.remedy: Configure the github-mcp-server entry in the repository's Copilot MCP settings with a personal access token or GitHub App and without /readonly, and select only the write tools the flow needs. Remember the agent still cannot merge, approve or mark its pull request ready.

rules.summary: The plugin declares an MCP server. An Actions session uses the MCP servers in the repository's Copilot configuration, supports only their tools, not resources or prompts, and a secret a server needs must be named COPILOT_MCP_*.
rules.remedy: Add the server to the repository's Copilot MCP configuration, with its secrets as COPILOT_MCP_* Agents secrets.

rules.summary: The plugin declares a remote (http or sse) MCP server with no static headers and no headersHelper, which usually means it authenticates by OAuth. For MCP servers configured in repository settings or custom agent profiles, the cloud agent does not support OAuth remotes.
rules.remedy: Use a server that takes a token in a header, from a COPILOT_MCP_* secret.
rules.notes: That a remote with no headers authenticates by OAuth is the scanner's inference; a public, unauthenticated server looks the same. That the cloud agent does not support OAuth remotes configured in repository settings or custom agent profiles is documented.

rules.summary: The cloud agent's firewall is on by default. It always allows the GitHub and Copilot hosts the agent uses, and a recommended allowlist, also on by default, covers common package registries, container registries, OS package repositories and certificate authorities. This host is on neither.
rules.remedy: Add the host as a custom allowlist rule in the repository's Copilot Internet access settings (an organization can lock this). Start a new session after the change.
rules.notes: allow is the Copilot in the cloud recommended allowlist as published on the checked date, plus github.com, api.github.com, *.github.com and *.githubcopilot.com for the GitHub and Copilot hosts the firewall always allows. An organization or repository can turn the recommended list off.

rules.summary: A command reads a credential from the environment. An Actions session gets secrets and variables from the repository's Agents secrets.
rules.remedy: Add the credential as an Agents secret or variable on the repository, under the name the command reads.

rules.summary: A flow that stops and waits for the person. An Actions session is non-interactive: nobody answers, and the session runs to its end.

match.look_for: Instructions to stop and wait for the user's answer, approval or choice before continuing: 'stop and ask', 'wait for the user', 'do not proceed without', a checkpoint after each step.

rules.remedy: Take every decision as an argument or from committed config, and end the session with a report of what a person has to decide.

rules.summary: In Actions-based and cloud sandbox sessions alike, Copilot works on one branch at a time and opens one pull request per task.

match.look_for: A flow that opens more than one pull request, works on more than one branch, or creates and deletes branches as it goes.

rules.remedy: One unit of work per session: let the cloud agent's own branch and pull request be the output.

rules.summary: An Actions session works in one repository.

match.look_for: A flow that reads or changes repositories other than the one the session started in.

rules.remedy: Split the work per repository, one session each.

rules.summary: An Actions session is prepared by .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml: one job named copilot-setup-steps, with timeout-minutes of at most 59, on a standard, larger or self-hosted runner. The file must be on the default branch.

match.look_for: A CLI, runtime or daemon the flow needs that a stock environment lacks (dagger, a database, a container engine), or a step that assumes something was installed before the session started.

rules.remedy: Install what the flow needs in the copilot-setup-steps job of .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml.

rules.summary: An Actions session runs for at most 59 minutes.

match.look_for: A flow expected to run longer than an hour end to end, or a wait bounded beyond what is left of the hour (for example a wait bounded at two hours, or several five-minute waits re-run in a loop).

rules.remedy: Cut the flow into pieces that each finish within the hour, with state carried in the repository or the pull request.
